doc_summary: The document is an index of Evan Hubinger's shortform comments. The text is mostly metadata, with a few quoted fragments on alignment evaluations losing evidential value, agentic misalignment work as a binary search for the most realistic settings, and avoiding an 'Everything-Bagel' failure mode in AI safety.

items.claim: Believes alignment evaluations are losing evidential value as models become more capable of recognizing tests, so he prefers treating eval results as weak evidence over taking them at face value.
items.quote: we are increasingly entering the regime where alignment evaluations will provide almost no evidence

items.claim: Argues that auditing and evaluation work should be reoriented to prepare for a world where reliable alignment audits are no longer available.
items.quote: However, I think this is suggestive that we should be reorienting a lot of model auditing and evaluation work to prepare for a world where we no longer have reliable alignment audi...

items.claim: Sees the saga of the model he held for two months as evidence that alignment auditing and evaluation are breaking down and will likely keep breaking down.
items.quote: I think this whole saga is pretty suggestive of ways in which alignment auditing and evaluation are breaking down and are likely to continue breaking down.

items.claim: Frames agentic misalignment work as one step in a binary search for the most realistic settings in which models still behave misaligned, rather than as a single definitive scenario.
items.quote: One way to think about our agentic misalignment work is as a single step in an ongoing binary search

items.claim: Prefers staying focused on the core catastrophic risks over an 'Everything-Bagel' approach that tries to cover every possible harm, because a scattered agenda becomes unviable.
items.quote: I think it's important to keep your eye on the ball and not become too susceptible to an Everything-Bagel failure mode
